text: {"score":3,"justification":"Headline and core numbers are accurate and grounded in the card and tool outputs, and the language is cautious. But the summary has internal tension and weak supporting evidence. It says 'Charts mostly support billing' while also reporting a 10.1% vs 2.4% share, and it never explains why the leaning is inconclusive. The 1-of-19 documented 99215 figure is thin evidence. Cited examples are weak: the one documentation example is the below-billed claim, and the two low-complexity examples have no chart record. Next steps are generic, naming the same three claims without a sample size and without including the high-complexity or supported claims for contrast. An investigator would have to redo some analysis.","problems":["'Charts mostly support billing' sits awkwardly beside the 4.1x excess 99215 share; the summary does not reconcile the two, and the rationale for 'inconclusive' is not explained.","Documentation evidence is thin: only 1 of 19 documented 99215 claims is below the billed level, and the 5% vs 7% comparison is not interpreted for significance.","Low-complexity examples C0067913 and C0068252 have no documentation attached, so they do not show chart mismatch; the next step to request charts for them is fine but generic.","Next steps do not specify sample size, selection method (e.g., the 25 low-complexity 99215 claims) or what to look for in the charts.","Omits the by-complexity gradient, and z vs peers of 1.02 is mentioned without explaining why it conflicts with the risk-adjusted score of 9.58.","The 'data' signal (7 of 29 moderate+ data notes without a lab line) is mentioned but not tied to specific claims; the note examples (e.g., C0068621) are not cited.","Does not flag missing results (MISSING_RESULTS deficiency in both rounds) as a limitation."]}
